title: Bandits with increasing concave means in calendar time and a known variation budget.
summary: All arms evolve with calendar time, including unpulled arms. Their fixed unknown means are increasing and concave in time. The learner sees only a fresh reward from the selected arm and competes with the current best mean. The variation budget is known.

task.formulation: All arms evolve with calendar time, including unpulled arms. Their fixed unknown means are increasing and concave in time. The learner sees only a fresh reward from the selected arm and competes with the current best mean. The variation budget is known.

description_paragraphs: All arms evolve with calendar time, including unpulled arms. Their fixed unknown means are increasing and concave in time. The learner sees only a fresh reward from the selected arm and competes with the current best mean. The variation budget is known.

model.instance: The reward laws $\nu_i(t)$ of the $K\ge2$ arms are fixed before interaction and evolve with absolute time, including for unpulled arms. Their means satisfy $$\mu_i(t)=\mathbb E_{X\sim\nu_i(t)}X\in[0,1],\qquad \gamma_i(t)=\mu_i(t+1)-\mu_i(t)\ge0.$$ and are discretely concave in time: $$\gamma_i(t+1)\le\gamma_i(t).$$ $$V_\mu=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\max_{i\in[K]}\gamma_i(t)\le V,\qquad 0\le V\le K.$$

operations.query_signature: Choose $I_t\in[K]$ from past observations and observe only $X_{I_t,t}$. Other arms' rewards are hidden. Each $X_{i,t}$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian around $\mu_i(t)$ and independent of the reward table before round $t$. Within-round dependence across arms is permitted. Only reward means are constrained to $[0,1]$; realizations need not lie there. Causal bandit policies are allowed and $K,T,\sigma,V$ is public. Mean functions and, for the concave model, change times are hidden. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

bounds.derivation: Lemma 3.1 in Appendix B uses a fixed hard prior, independent of the algorithm and uniform over the best arm in each window. This transfer follows from the appendix construction, rather than only from an extension stated in a footnote.
